card.name: Words leading into observational study descriptions
card.fires_on: Words just before a study-design noun such as analysis, study or studies, in citations and research summaries about cancer and diet risk. Often the word is prospective, pooled, a number, or a researcher group.

modes.label: Study-design adjective
modes.description: An adjective like prospective or pooled that comes right before a study or analysis noun.
modes.example: A large<< prospective>> 10 year observational cohort study conducted

modes.label: Number or 'of' before studies
modes.description: A number or the word of that precedes a count or type of studies being pooled.
modes.example: Alcohol and breast cancer in women: a pooled analysis<< of>> cohort studies.

modes.label: Researchers evaluating data
modes.description: A word naming the researchers or study group just before they evaluated or followed data.
modes.example: Susanna C. Larsson of the Karolinska Institute and<< colleagues>> evaluated data from 82,0

card.writes: It pushes toward words like correlations, analyses, retrospective and correlate, and away from experiment words.
card.plain: It fires where a sentence is about to describe an observational or pooled study rather than a lab experiment.
